title: Burst reserve burndown: token-to-hire ladder probe
body:
Purpose:
Quick exploratory sheet to link short-term token demand/burst needs to an actionable hiring ladder and price-sensitivity triggers. Not a final proforma — used for partner sync and ops-runbook inputs.

Assumptions (baseline):
- Baseline hosted token volume (q1 2026): 6B tokens/mo.
- Avg revenue per 1k tokens (baseline price): $0.006 per token => $6 per 1k tokens (note: internal units).
- Unit GPU cost (amortized infra + ops) per 1k tokens = $2.75.
- Average tokens per routed request: 900.
- FTE throughput proxy: 1 infra engineer + 1 SRE pair supports ~60M tokens/day of steady-state serving (including overhead).
- Hiring lead time: 10 weeks ramp to full productivity for infra/SRE; 16 weeks for senior infra engineers.

Mini-table: scenario-level quick calcs (rows = scenarios)
Columns: Scenario | Token growth % over baseline | Price per 1k tokens ($) | Expected margin per 1k ($) | FTE add (prob-weighted) | Hiring trigger (tokens/mo) | Immediate ops spend delta ($/mo) | Notes

1) Courtesy spike (1.2x) | 20% | 6.0 | 3.25 | 0.5 FTE | 7.2B | +$55k | Use burst reserve; avoid hires if <8w sustained
2) Sustained growth (1.5x) | 50% | 6.0 | 3.25 | 3.0 FTE | 9.0B | +$330k | Start rolling hires Q3; prioritize infra generalists
3) Price shock (demand responds) | 50% growth projected but price cut to $5/1k | 50% growth -> price down to $5 | margin per 1k = 2.25 | 4.2 FTE | 9.0B | +$360k | Lower margin increases FTE need; consider targeted price increases for high-margin cohorts
4) Elasticity high (demand falls with price up) | -20% | 7.5 | margin = 4.75 | -1.0 FTE (defer hires) | 4.8B | -$60k | Put hiring freeze triggers if two consecutive months negative growth
5) Burst-heavy enterprise wins | +120% concentrated bursts | 120% | 6.5 | 6.5 FTE (capacity + ops) | 13.2B peak | +$1.1M | Designated reserved pool + temporary contractors

Quick notes on FTE math (back-of-envelope):
- Convert token delta to daily throughput then to FTE by 60M tokens/day per FTE proxy.
- Example: 6B baseline -> 200M tokens/day. 50% growth -> +100M/day -> ~1.7 FTE additional; add 75% buffer for ops complexity -> ~3.0 FTE.

Probability-weighted hiring ladder (example):
- We estimate 3-month probability for scenarios: Courtesy spike 0.35, Sustained growth 0.25, Price shock 0.15, Elasticity high 0.10, Burst-heavy enterprise 0.15.
- Expected hires (3mo weighted) = sum(p * FTE_add) = 0.35*0.5 + 0.25*3.0 + 0.15*4.2 + 0.10*(-1.0) + 0.15*6.5 = 0.175 + 0.75 + 0.63 -0.10 +0.975 = 2.43 FTE -> round plan to 2-3 hires over next quarter (mix contractors + perm).

Microbudget corridors & runbooks (operational levers):
- Corridor A (0–10% growth): use burst reserve credits + transient contractors (cost cap $70k/mo), defer perm hires.
- Corridor B (10–40%): hire 1 infra generalist + 1 ops engineer (contractor to perm plan). Budget mid: $200–$300k/mo incremental.
- Corridor C (40%+ sustained): open recruitment for senior infra (2) and SRE leads (1); pre-approve budget up to $500k/mo incremental and initiate capacity commit with cloud partner.

Pricing sensitivity checklist (to feed product/CS):
- Identify top 10 customers by token share; run per-customer elasticity experiment before price increases.
- Offer tiered reservations (committed burst credits) at a small discount to de-risk hiring.
- Use feature flags to throttle non-SLA traffic if unit margin < $1.5/1k tokens.

Triggers (operational):
- 2 consecutive months >20% MoM increase -> trigger Corridor B hires + capacity commit request.
- Any single month >80% peak spike causing 95th pct latency breach -> emergency burst pool + hire contractor SRE (2–6 week window).
- Sustained 3-month weighted expected FTE > 2.0 -> open 3 perm reqs (staggered).

Open questions / To-do:
- Validate FTE throughput proxy with infra bench team (ping: infra-perf).
- Get contract rates for 6–12 week SRE burst support (target $120–180/hr).
- Build quick per-customer elasticity probe: sample 20 accounts for 2-week price A/B. Owner: Maya.
- Map current reserved capacity SLA headroom (dedicated pools) and cost to projected Corridor C.

Appendix: raw sensitivity quick calc (cells)
- Baseline revenue = tokens/1k * price_per_1k. Example: 6B tokens -> 6,000,000 1k units * $6 = $36,000,000/mo.
- Baseline infra cost = 6,000,000 * $2.75 = $16,500,000/mo. Gross margin = $19,500,000 -> margin per 1k = $3.25.
- Incremental cost for hiring: assume fully loaded cost per FTE (hire + comp + benefits + infra) = $35k/mo.
- For burst contractor overlay assume $150/hr * 160 hrs/mo = $24k/mo per contractor.

Bottom line recommendation (short):
- Convert this probe into a living sheet that product and infra update weekly.
- Approve $250k of burst-reserve & contractor budget for H1 to avoid reactive perm hiring.
- Run 2-week price elasticity A/B on top 20 customers before making permanent price moves.

Editors: Ava (lead), Diego (ops calcs), Maya (customer elasticity).
